statement.excerpt: NVIDIA does not magically have more demand for its GPUs. In fact, it has less thanks to the Huang affair leading to the closure of a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent NVIDIA GPUs remotely from countries like Malaysia,

from_speaker: Chinese firms to rent NVIDIA GPUs remotely
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that restrictions prompted by the affair reduced demand for NVIDIA GPUs relative to what demand would otherwise have been. This does not necessarily mean quarterly sales fell.
The causal chain requires evidence connecting the affair to the restrictions and the restrictions to lost GPU business.
The described episode is the current November 2026 controversy, through the post date.
A canceled rental contract establishes lost business for that arrangement. It does not by itself establish lower aggregate demand for NVIDIA GPUs if customers or capacity move elsewhere.
criteria.support_condition: Dated records connect the affair to implemented remote-access restrictions and show that those restrictions reduced NVIDIA GPU orders or demand, with enough information to distinguish lost demand from relocated business.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Records establish that the claimed restrictions did not occur, that the affair did not contribute to them, or that affected business was replaced or relocated without reducing NVIDIA GPU demand.
